messages:
maya: Heads-up — we need to coordinate a base-image rebuild for runtime boot-chain hardening. Goal: KMS-backed image signing, kubelet-level verification, tightened node-agent RBAC, and structured audit logs to the SIEM. Who can own the orchestration?

carl: I'm happy to own orchestration and rollout for eng-runtime. Need SRE / infra help for canaries and traffic shaping.

anya: SRE can handle the canary plan. Questions: 1) which KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) do we target first, 2) what does the backout look like if nodes fail to boot verification?

maya: Prefer starting with GCP KMS because most of dedicated infra lives in us-central1. Backout: we must keep an unsigned fallback image pinned in the nodepool autoscaler as a last-resort; also kubelet flag toggle to disable enforcement remotely. We should document the rollback commands.

luis: For RBAC, node-agent needs a minimal IAM role to fetch verification keys from KMS/public key material only — not decrypt. We'll propose creating a short-lived Workload Identity binding: `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/images/cryptoKeys/cosign` (read-only), and a separate admin role for signing ops.

maya: Good. Also want to ensure signing keys are HSM-backed and rotation is in the playbook. We'll use cosign with KMS URIs. Example signing command for reference:

```
# sign with GCP KMS
cosign sign --key gcpkms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/images/cryptoKeys/cosign \
  gcr.io/redwood/base-runtime:v4.2.0
```

carl: Nice. On the runtime side we'll add a validation hook in the node bootstrap: verify image signature before pivot_root. If verification fails, node logs to journald and increments a cluster-level alert metric. We'll throttle new node creation during rollout to 2 nodes/min.

auditor-bot: Note: For compliance we need structured audit events for: image-signature-verified, key-id, signer-identity, verification-result, node-id, and timestamp. Route to /audit/images and retain for 2 years.

anya: We'll need a test harness that simulates bad signatures and key rotation mid-roll. Can SRE + eng-runtime pair on that? Also want a chaos checklist for stuck nodes.

carl: Yes — build a k8s Job that boots nodes in a VM with signed/unsigned images and asserts kubelet behavior. We'll add an e2e: `tests/boot-verify/*` in repo.

maya: Vulnerability triage note: before rebuild, run a full SBOM diff against current images and block unpatched OS packages with CVSS > 7 unless mitigated. If we find critical CVEs that require kernel updates, we should pause signing until the patched image is ready.

luis: Agreed. Also adding an attestation layer: store cosign provenance in an internal attestations DB, keyed by image digest, with signed predicate. That helps incident response (who signed what, when).

maya: Timeline proposal: Week A — create key rings, RBAC roles, and signing pipeline; Week B — produce signed images + SBOM + unit tests; Week C — canary rollout to dev/staging nodepools; Week D — gradual prod rollout. Risk review and approval at end of Week B.

anya: Ops windows? Recommend low-traffic Wednesday 02:00–06:00 UTC for prod canary and 02:00–10:00 for full rollout. We'll open pager for first 24h post-rollout.

carl: I'll draft the runbook and rollback commands. Quick checklist for reviewers: 1) Verify KMS key policy (no unapproved principals), 2) RBAC least privilege, 3) audit events wired, 4) SBOM diffs reviewed, 5) canary health thresholds (error rate < 0.2% and boot success > 99%).

maya: Can @luis and @anya sign off on roles and canary plan by EOD Friday? Also tag product-security for the compliance sign-off.

luis: I'll create the IAM proposals in git: `infra/iam/base-image-signing.md` and link the KMS ARNs. ETA Friday noon.

anya: I'll write the canary playbook and tests, link PR by Friday 17:00.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: base-image-signing-infra (PR 4821) -> staging apply at 2061124200, prod apply at 2061200000.

maya: Great. After sign-off we'll run a tabletop incident sim for the abort/backout flow. Last Q: do we want to require cosign verification at kubelet or at the image-puller layer (containerd)? containerd-level check blocks earlier; kubelet-level gives more flexibility. Thoughts?

carl: Prefer containerd-layer verification where possible (pre-pull), but add kubelet fallback enforcement. Implement both: containerd plugin for pre-pull policy, kubelet flag for enforcement.

maya: Perfect. I'll file the compliance ticket and update the sprint board. Thanks everyone — let's reconvene after the PRs land. :thumbsup:
